Far from Chaos
This army's daemons are far from the magic of Chaos. They can hold their form a little longer, and are sustained again as soon as they reach land that Chaos has corrupted.
Fading Daemons

This army's daemons have been away from the magic of Chaos for too long, and they are fading. They will weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last slip back into the Realm of Chaos, one unit at a time. Land that Chaos has corrupted stops the fading at once. The army's lords and heroes are not affected.
Daemons Held by Magic
The Chaos Invasion or strong Winds of Magic keep this army's daemons from fading. While that lasts, they grow no weaker, but only land that Chaos has corrupted can restore them.
Far from the Horned Rat
This army's Verminlords are far from the corruption of the Horned Rat. They can hold their form a little longer, and are sustained again as soon as they reach land the Skaven have corrupted.
Fading Verminlords

This army's Verminlords have been away from the corruption of the Horned Rat for too long, and they are fading. They will weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last slip back into the Realm of Chaos, one unit at a time. Land the Skaven have corrupted stops the fading at once.
Verminlords Held by Magic
The Vermintide or strong Winds of Magic keep this army's Verminlords from fading. While that lasts, they grow no weaker, but only land the Skaven have corrupted can restore them.
Far from Death's Magic

This army's undead are far from the magic of death that binds them. They can hold together a little longer, and that magic takes hold of them again as soon as they reach land tainted by vampiric corruption.
Crumbling Undead

This army's undead have been away from the magic of death for too long, and they are falling apart. They will weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last crumble to dust, one unit at a time. Land tainted by vampiric corruption stops this at once. The army's lords and heroes are not affected.
Undead Held by Magic
Nagash's return or strong Winds of Magic keep this army's undead from fading. While that lasts, they grow no weaker, but only land tainted by vampiric corruption can restore them.
Far from Friendly Land

This army's Tomb Kings units are far from friendly land, and the incantations that bind them are weakening. The units can hold together a little longer, and the incantations take hold again as soon as the units reach land held by their own faction or an ally.
Failing Bindings

This army's Tomb Kings units have been away from friendly land for too long, and the incantations that bind them are failing. These units will weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last fall still, one unit at a time. Land held by their own faction or an ally stops this at once. The army's lords and heroes are not affected.
Bindings Held by Magic
A Storm of Magic or Nagash's return keeps this army's Tomb Kings units from fading. While that lasts, they grow no weaker, but only land held by their own faction or an ally can restore them.
Far from Clean Land
This army's spirits are far from the clean land that sustains them. They can endure a little longer, and are safe again as soon as they reach land where corruption is light.
Withering Spirits

This army's spirits have been away from clean land for too long, and they are withering. They will weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last be lost, one unit at a time. Land where corruption is light stops this at once. The army's lords and heroes are not affected.
Spirits Held by Magic
A Storm of Magic keeps this army's spirits from fading. While it lasts, they grow no weaker, but only land where corruption is light can restore them.
Creatures of Magic
Some of your daemons, undead, Tomb Kings units or spirits have begun to fade.

Daemons are sustained by land that Chaos has corrupted, the undead by vampiric corruption, spirits by clean land, and Tomb Kings units by land held by their own faction or an ally. Away from that land, these units hold out for a few turns. Then they weaken, stop regaining their strength and at last desert. Lords and heroes are never affected. Check an army's effects to see how long its units can hold out.

Daemons, undead and spirits
Daemons, undead and spirits need their land

Daemons need land that Chaos has corrupted, and the undead need land tainted by vampiric corruption. Spirits, such as the Wood Elves' tree spirits, need clean land. Tomb Kings units need land held by their faction or an ally. Away from their land, these units hold out for a few turns. Then they weaken as a hungry army does. They lose strength, stop regaining it, and finally desert. Lords and heroes are never affected. Off: these units need nothing. CA's Vampire Counts factions never suffer the game's own attrition outside vampiric land, even with this switched off. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
Other armies need their land

Armies of factions that no player controls follow the same rule while Other factions use their stores is on. Off: only your own armies do. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
Strong magic holds them

Strong or Tempestuous Winds of Magic keep daemons and the undead from fading. A Storm of Magic keeps all of these units from fading, spirits and Tomb Kings units included. The Chaos Invasion keeps daemons from fading, and Nagash's return keeps the undead and Tomb Kings units from fading. Off: only their own land helps them. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
Turns before they fade

How many turns these units can spend away from their land before they start to fade. They first lose strength two turns after that. Their own land gives them back the full number of turns at once. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
Corruption they need

How much corruption a region needs to sustain daemons and the undead. Daemons count every kind of Chaos corruption, and the undead count vampiric corruption. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
Most corruption spirits can bear
The most corruption a region can have and still sustain spirits, counting every kind together. You can change this during a campaign. The change applies from your next turn.
